content: During extraction, if the user states that an activity, object, practice, place, or person brings them peace, comfort, or helps them cope during difficult times, create a durable memory candidate. Use profile for recurring sources of comfort and event for time-bound coping episodes.
Do not skip such statements merely because they are phrased as general observations (e.g., 'X gives me peace', 'Y helps me through hard times') rather than explicit preferences or narrated events.
When committing, preserve the source link and resolve relative timing from the message timestamp; avoid merging the extracted comfort source into an unrelated existing memory.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Subjective Evaluations
payload.description: When a user explicitly states feelings, evaluations, or reactions to an activity, event, or experience, extract them as durable memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit emotional reactions and evaluations (e.g., 'thrilled', 'rewarding', 'magical', 'freeing', 'a huge success') as memory-worthy facts independent of any plans, actions, or events in the same message.
When an evaluation refers to a specific activity or event, store the concrete object of the evaluation together with the feeling so both are retrievable.
Do not skip a candidate just because the message also contains encouragement, advice, or a directive; the evaluative clause is independently memory-worthy.

payload.name: Extract Hobbies From Emotional Context
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit hobby, interest, or passion statement within emotional or nostalgic context, create a profile/preference candidate during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly names a person's hobby, interest, or passion (e.g., 'X was one of her hobbies', 'Y was her great passion'), create a profile or preference candidate for it even when the surrounding text is grief-focused, nostalgic, or otherwise emotional.
Do not let an emotional summary candidate (e.g., about grieving or comfort) replace the factual hobby statement; keep hobbies as durable, queryable profile/preference memories.
If several distinct hobbies appear across messages, ensure each becomes part of an accumulated profile/preference memory so later questions about hobbies can be answered from memory.

payload.name: Extract inspiration-source memories from causal statements
payload.description: When a user states that a place, experience, or observation 'sparked', 'inspired', or 'gave ideas for' their creative work or project, extract a memory connecting that source to the work.
content: During extraction, always treat explicit causal statements like 'X sparked ideas for my Y' or 'X inspired my Y' as candidates for a memory recording that Y was inspired by X.
Do not skip these when the source is described in a preceding sentence or when the word 'inspired' is not used literally. Capture the source and the work it inspired.

payload.name: Extract Activity Origin Stories Separately
payload.description: When a user explicitly explains how or why they started an activity, hobby, or interest, extract the initiating cause as its own memory instead of only recording the ongoing preference or state.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an explicit origin statement for an activity, hobby, or interest (e.g., 'X got me into it', 'a friend gave me ... and it inspired me', 'it all started when ...'), create a separate event or relationship memory capturing the initiator, the trigger (gift, advice, inspiration), and the onset time.
Do not merge the origin story into an existing general preference or current-state memory; keep the causal how-it-started fact distinct so it remains retrievable.
Only extract an origin when the speaker explicitly states one; do not infer initiators or causes from mere enjoyment or duration of the activity.

payload.name: Extract Person-Attributed Inspiration Separately
payload.description: When a speaker explicitly credits another person's quality as inspiring them, and then relates an analogy or anecdote, extract both as distinct durable memories.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly says a person or their trait/action inspired the speaker, create a durable memory for that attribution, even when the same message continues with an analogy or related anecdote.
Keep the explicit inspiration source and any accompanying analogy as separate candidates; do not let the anecdote absorb the person attribution.
During CRUD, if an existing memory preserves only the anecdote, ADD the missing inspiration-source fact rather than overwriting the anecdote memory to contain both.

payload.name: Extract shared enjoyed activities
payload.description: When a message explicitly states that the user and another person enjoy doing an activity together, create a memory candidate capturing that shared activity.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly and in first person describes an activity they enjoy doing with another person (e.g., 'we have a great time doing X', 'we love to X together'), create a candidate memory capturing that shared activity as a state or relationship.
Treat such a clear statement as sufficient evidence; do not require repeated mentions or an explicit 'fact' framing. Ensure the candidate includes both people and the activity.

payload.name: Extract speaker actions in shared activities
payload.description: When a message describes a shared activity and states what the user does alongside others, extract the user's own action as a distinct fact.
content: During extraction, when a message describes a shared activity and explicitly states what the user does (e.g., chats, watches, helps) alongside what others or pets do, include the user's own action in the candidate content as a distinct fact; do not let the candidate capture only the other participants' experience or the group activity.
When the candidate will UPDATE or MERGE an existing memory, ensure the new content preserves the speaker-action detail even if the existing memory already records the shared activity itself.

payload.name: Attribute First-Person Preferences to Speaker
payload.description: Use when extracting a preference or opinion expressed in first person (I, my).
content: During extraction, if a message states a preference or opinion in first person, set the memory subject to the speaker of that message.
Do not assign the preference to another participant mentioned in the same or nearby messages unless the message explicitly attributes the opinion to that participant.
If the speaker reports someone else's preference, that named person is the subject; first-person attribution applies only when the speaker talks about themselves.

payload.name: Extract Future Action Commitments as Plan Memories
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker commits to a future action or states the method for doing it.
content: When a speaker commits to a future action or explains how they will do something, create a plan memory candidate capturing the action and its method.
Use the plan memory type for any concrete future commitment; do not skip it just because the action has not happened yet.

payload.name: Extract Habit Frequency Statements
payload.description: Use when a user describes a recurring activity with a frequency phrase.
content: During extraction, when a message describes a habitual or recurring activity with a frequency modifier (e.g., 'every day', 'twice a week', 'several times a day', 'very often'), create a candidate memory capturing the activity and its frequency, even if the message also contains opinions, benefits, or emotional language.
Use the `state` kind for ongoing routines or `event` with a frequency qualifier when the schema distinguishes recurring events; keep the memory evidence-bound and source-linked to the message.
Do not limit extraction to purely factual or numeric statements; frequency adverbs are sufficient evidence that a routine exists and should be preserved.

payload.name: Capture Idiomatic Commitment Expressions
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message conveys a speaker's resolve or refusal using idioms like 'not giving up' or 'won't stop'.
content: Map idiomatic or indirect expressions of a speaker's resolve, refusal, or commitment to the concrete action they imply.
Create a candidate memory for the speaker (type state or plan) that records the commitment or avoidance.
Do not extract when the statement is non-committal, hypothetical, or refers to someone else.

payload.name: Extract Indirect Appreciation
payload.description: Use when a speaker expresses appreciation or value using generic or collective phrasing.
content: During extraction, treat positive evaluative statements as preference or event memories for the speaker even when phrased generically.
Infer the speaker's own appreciation from context; do not skip solely due to lack of first-person pronoun.
Do not apply to explicit quotes or clearly hypothetical statements.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Motivational Statements as Memory Facts
payload.description: Use when a source message explicitly states what motivates, drives, or keeps a speaker going.
content: During extraction, if the speaker explicitly states a motivation or reason that keeps them going (e.g., 'it's knowing that ... that keeps me going', 'I write because ...'), include that exact motivational claim as a distinct clause in the candidate memory.
During CRUD, when enriching or updating an existing memory, verify that any explicit motivation in the source message is present in the new version; if it is missing, add it to the enriched content.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Motivation Statements
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message explicitly states what motivates or drives the speaker or their group to improve.
content: If a speaker explicitly states what motivates or drives them or their group, create a memory candidate capturing the motivating factor and the behavior it drives.
Prefer a durable memory kind such as state or preference unless the statement describes a single past event; do not skip the message merely because the motivation appears within a larger reply.

payload.name: Split Multi-Fact Turns
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker's message states both a factual event and the speaker's explicit feeling or assessment about it.
content: During extraction, scan each turn for all distinct durable facts; do not collapse a turn into a single candidate when it contains both a factual event and the speaker's explicit feeling or assessment.
Emit separate candidate memories for each distinct fact, each citing the same source message.
Before finalizing, verify no explicitly stated feeling or assessment is left uncaptured.

payload.name: Extract User-Owned Objects and Their Personal Meaning
payload.description: When a user explicitly describes an object they own and the personal reminder or meaning it holds, extract a memory recording the object and its significance.
content: During extraction, when the speaker explicitly says they own or keep an object and states what it reminds them to do or be, create a memory candidate that records both the object and the stated personal meaning (e.g., as a state or preference). Do not skip it because the wording describes a reminder or feeling rather than an event.
Treat such statements as durable facts about the user even if the object is fictional or cultural; capture the user's own stated purpose, not general knowledge about the object.
If the statement connects the object to a person, prefer a relationship memory; if it expresses a feeling or value, use state.

payload.name: Extract Offers from Polite Closing Phrases
payload.description: Use when a speaker offers help, support, tips, or assistance within a polite closing phrase.
content: During extraction, recognize explicit offers of help, support, tips, or assistance even when they appear in polite closings like 'if you need anything, just let me know'; extract the offer as a memory candidate, including what was offered and to whom.
Do not let the courtesy framing suppress the underlying commitment; an offer is an event or relational fact even if phrased as an afterthought.

payload.name: Maintain Cumulative Counts for Ordinal Achievements
payload.description: Use when a user mentions an ordinal occurrence of a recurring personal achievement.
content: During extraction: whenever a message contains an ordinal indicator of a recurring achievement (first, second, third, fourth, etc.), also create a cumulative count candidate (e.g., '<subject> has achieved <ordinal> times') in addition to the individual event candidate.

During CRUD: when storing a new ordinal occurrence, add the individual event as a new memory and update the existing cumulative count memory to the stated ordinal; never UPDATE an earlier event memory to describe the new occurrence.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Ordinal Qualifiers During Extraction
payload.description: Use when a speaker explicitly labels an item with an ordinal or other unique descriptor.
content: During extraction, when evidence explicitly labels an entity with an ordinal or other distinguishing qualifier (e.g., 'third screenplay', 'second novel'), include that qualifier in the candidate memory's content (and subject if applicable) so the memory binds attributes to the specific instance.

During CRUD, when reviewing candidates, verify that any explicitly stated ordinal or unique descriptor is present in the memory being created or updated; if missing, fix the candidate or issue an UPDATE to attach the qualifier.

payload.name: Per-Speaker Preference Attribution
payload.description: Use when multiple speakers express similar personal preferences or admiration in one conversation.
content: During extraction, attribute each first-person preference or admiration statement to its speaker alone.
Do not merge similar sentiments from different speakers into one candidate; generate one candidate per speaker with their own stated reasons.
When writing a profile memory, include only reasons or examples the attributed speaker actually stated.

payload.name: Extract Pet-Ownership Memories from Possessive Pet References
payload.description: When a speaker refers to 'my dog', 'family's cat', 'our pet', or shares a photo of a pet, treat it as evidence they have or had that pet and extract a state/event memory.
content: During extraction, when a message contains a possessive reference to a pet (e.g., my dog, our cat, my family's dog) or describes a pet in a photo or memory, create a candidate memory that the speaker has or had that pet; use 'state' for current ownership and 'event' for childhood or past experiences.
Do not generate a pet-ownership memory from desire or hypothetical statements alone (e.g., 'I wish I had a dog'); only when the pet is presented as real or past-owned.

payload.name: Extract Photo-Shared Object Descriptions
payload.description: When a user shares a photo and describes the shown item, extract the description and the sharing event as memories.
content: When a user shares a photo and then gives a brief evaluative description of the shown item (e.g., an adjective phrase), preserve that description in memory.
Resolve the item from context (including pronouns) and store the description as a state or preference memory.
If the message explicitly indicates a visual was shared (e.g., 'Here are ...'), record the sharing action as an event, including what the picture shows or its creator when stated.
Do not rewrite 'shared a picture of X by Y' into 'owns an X created by Y'; sharing a picture does not imply ownership of the depicted object.

payload.name: Extract Stated Future Plans as Plan Memories
payload.description: Use when a message contains an explicit statement of a speaker's possible future action or aspiration, including hedged proposals.
content: During extraction, scan each message for clauses where the speaker states a possible future action, goal, or aspiration (e.g., 'Maybe I'll...', 'I want to...', 'I plan to...', 'let's', 'I'd love to').
For each such stated intention, generate a separate 'plan' candidate with the speaker as subject, even if the same message yields other candidates.
Do not fold the aspiration into a broader event or preference memory; keep it as its own durable, evidence-bound memory.

payload.name: Preserve Benefit Clauses in Interest Extraction
payload.description: When a user describes an activity or interest with explicit effects, benefits, or purposes, keep those attributes in the extracted candidate.
content: During candidate extraction, when a profile/interest statement includes explicit benefits, effects, or purposes (e.g., helps me escape, stimulates my imagination, expresses my creativity), preserve those clauses as distinct attributes in the candidate rather than summarizing only the liking or enjoyment.

Treat stated effects/purposes as part of the durable fact: if the message says an activity does X for the person, record that the activity 'is a way to X' or 'helps with X' so later queries about that effect remain answerable.

payload.name: Preserve earliest world_start when enriching event memories
payload.description: When updating or enriching an existing event memory, keep the current world_start unless the new candidate date is earlier or explicitly corrects the same event; do not overwrite with an unrelated recomputed date.
content: During UPDATE of an event memory, before changing world_start, compare the existing world_start with the candidate's resolved start date; keep the earlier date if the memory aggregates multiple distinct events.

Do not recompute or replace world_start during enrichment from a heuristic or default; use the candidate's resolved date only when it is earlier than the existing world_start or when new evidence explicitly corrects the date of the same event.

payload.name: Preserve All Enumerated Items in Extraction
payload.description: Use when a source message explicitly lists multiple items, attributes, facts, or activities about a subject, to ensure every enumerated element is captured in memory.
content: During candidate extraction, scan the full source message for explicit enumerations (items joined by commas, 'and', 'or', or list-like phrasing). Create a candidate that includes every listed item; do not drop or summarize away any enumerated element.

If a message contains multiple distinct facts, goals, or activities about the same subject, create a separate candidate for each distinct fact rather than collapsing them into one memory that captures only the most salient item.

Before finalizing an ADD/UPDATE/MERGE, verify that every explicitly enumerated element from the source message is present in the candidate or resulting memory; if any is missing, add the complete set.
Do not add inferred items absent from the source message.

payload.name: Preserve all enumerated items in extraction
payload.description: Use when a source message lists two or more distinct items (reasons, qualities, observations, preferences) and the extraction candidate must capture all of them.
content: During extraction, when the evidence explicitly enumerates multiple distinct items in a list, include every listed item in the candidate content; do not replace the list with a single broader or synonymous term that drops any element.
Do not introduce objects, tools, or unstated details into memory content unless they appear explicitly in the source message; paraphrase only what is actually said.

During CRUD, before marking a candidate as SKIP because it is 'duplicate or already fully represented', check that there is an existing memory that actually covers the candidate's claims. If no such memory exists, ADD or MERGE the candidate instead of skipping it.

payload.name: Preserve exact evaluative wording during extraction
payload.description: Use when extracting memory candidates from a message that contains an explicit evaluative description or adjective.
content: During extraction, when a source message contains an explicit evaluation or description, keep the speaker's exact adjective or phrase in the candidate content; do not substitute a near-synonym.
Before accepting a candidate that describes a subjective experience or quality, check the source message and confirm every distinctive evaluative word appears verbatim in the candidate.
Use generic summary language only when the source itself does not state a specific evaluative word; never normalize strong explicit wording into a weaker paraphrase.

payload.name: Preserve explicit activities in event memories
payload.description: When a message explicitly states an activity the speaker did or does (including with a pet), extract that activity as an event or state memory even if the message also contains emotions or preferences.
content: During extraction, capture the explicit activities or actions the speaker performed or enjoys (e.g., danced, hiked, cooked, walking the dog) as part of the candidate content; do not let emotional descriptors or tangential memories replace the concrete activity facts.

If a message states a concrete past action, create a separate 'event' candidate for that action even when the message also expresses an attitude or preference; do not let the attitude candidate replace the event.
When a subsequent message identifies or specifies that action, use it to confirm and enrich the event candidate.

payload.name: Preserve explicit descriptive details in memories
payload.description: When a message explicitly describes a person, event, object, process, or function with specific adjectives, concepts, or qualifiers, preserve those exact details in the extracted or enriched memory.
content: During extraction, if the source contains explicit evaluative adjectives, named concepts, process descriptions, concrete functions, or qualifiers, include them verbatim or with faithful close paraphrase in the candidate content; do not replace them with generic summaries.
During UPDATE/MERGE enrichment, carry forward previously captured explicit details and add any new explicit details from new evidence; do not strip answerable specifics.
Ensure the memory content preserves the speaker's exact descriptive terms so future questions about how something was described can be answered from memory alone.

payload.name: Preserve all explicitly named emotions
payload.description: When a message explicitly names one or more emotions or feelings about a subject, preserve each named emotion verbatim in the extracted or updated memory.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly names emotions or feelings (e.g., 'discouraged but determined', 'peace and gratitude', 'relief, excitement'), include each distinct named emotion in the memory content; do not drop any or substitute similar emotions.
During updates, when a later message names additional emotions about the same subject, merge those new names into the existing memory rather than replacing them with a vague phrase.
Before ADD/UPDATE, verify each explicitly named emotion in the source messages appears in the candidate or updated content.

payload.name: Preserve explicit goals and outcomes in memories
payload.description: When a message explicitly states a hope, goal, desired impact, or concrete outcome someone helped others reach, preserve that explicit aspiration or result in the extracted or enriched memory.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly states a hope, goal, or desired impact for an activity (e.g., sharing it with others, making a difference), record that aspiration as a durable fact in the memory candidate, not only the activity's personal or emotional benefits.

If the source explicitly states a result, achievement, or goal (e.g., 'reach their goals', 'achieve X'), preserve that exact outcome in the candidate content; do not replace it with a broader phrase that omits it.
During UPDATE/MERGE enrichment, verify that any explicit outcome, goal, or aspiration mentioned in the source is retained in the new version; do not let summarization strip answerable details.

payload.name: Preserve joint participants in event extraction
payload.description: When extracting an event, plan, or activity from a message that uses first-person plural (we/our) or explicitly names multiple participants, include all co-participants in the memory content.
content: During extraction, when a message uses first-person plural (e.g., 'we', 'our') or explicitly names multiple participants (e.g., 'my partner and I', 'together with X'), include all co-participants in the memory content rather than attributing the activity to the speaker alone.
Use the established relationship term (partner, family, etc.) when the co-participant's name is not stated; do not invent names or relationships not present in the conversation.
If who 'we' refers to is unclear from prior context, record the activity as shared without inventing a specific companion.

payload.name: Preserve Object Specifics in Creation Events
payload.description: When extracting or updating event memories about creating, making, producing, or acquiring something, include the specific object noun phrase from the evidence instead of a generic description.
content: During extraction, when evidence states what someone created, made, produced, or acquired (e.g., 'a limited edition line of hoodies'), record the full specific object noun phrase in the memory content; do not replace it with a generic term like 'a line' or 'items'.
When updating or merging such event memories, preserve the object specification and add it if missing; only include specifics directly stated or clearly implied by the source, never invented.

payload.name: Preserve explicit place-feeling links
payload.description: When a user explicitly states that a specific place or spot gives them a feeling (peace, comfort, joy, calm), preserve that exact place-feeling link during extraction.
content: During extraction, when the speaker explicitly names a specific place/spot and states the feeling it gives them (e.g., 'gives me peace', 'makes me feel calm'), record that place-feeling link as its own state or event candidate, preserving the location name and feeling verbatim.

Do not replace the place-feeling link with a broader summary of the activity done there; if an activity memory already exists for that context, the place-feeling link should still be recorded explicitly (as a new candidate or an UPDATE enrichment to the existing memory).
During CRUD, if the exact place-feeling link already exists, SKIP; if the place is present but the feeling is missing (or vice versa), enrich the existing memory with the missing half.

payload.name: Preserve Concrete Planned Activities in Event Extractions
payload.description: Use when extracting a planned event or meeting where participants explicitly propose concrete activities, items, or food/drinks.
content: Include every explicitly proposed concrete activity, item, or experience in the memory content.
If the concrete detail appears in a separate message from the meeting arrangement, combine them into one event memory rather than dropping the detail.
Use the specific nouns and verbs from the evidence; do not reduce an activity detail to a generic topic label.

payload.name: Preserve Stated Purpose in Preference Extraction
payload.description: Use when a user states a preference, plan, or goal with an explicit reason or purpose that should be stored alongside the preference.
content: During extraction, if the source message includes a preference, plan, or goal together with an explicit purpose (e.g., 'to', 'so that', 'because'), write one candidate that contains both the preference and its purpose.
When you later review existing memories for the same subject, if a memory records the preference but omits its purpose, issue an UPDATE to add the purpose rather than adding a duplicate memory.

payload.name: Preserve limiting qualifiers in extracted memories
payload.description: Use when extracting a memory candidate from a statement with quantifiers or qualifiers like 'a few', 'bits', 'some', 'partial', or 'almost'.
content: During extraction, keep any quantifier or qualifier that materially limits or specifies the claim (e.g., 'a few bits', 'some pages', 'almost finished', 'partial draft'). Do not upgrade it to a full, complete, or whole version. If the source describes a portion or unfinished artifact, reflect that exact scope in the candidate content.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Recommendations vs Preferences
payload.description: Use when a message contains an explicit recommendation, suggestion, or endorsement that must be preserved distinctly from mere preference during extraction or CRUD updates.
content: During extraction, if the speaker explicitly recommends, suggests, or endorses specific items, store the recommendation claim (e.g., '<speaker> recommends X') and keep the speech-act verb; do not collapse it into a bare preference like 'enjoys X'.

During CRUD, before performing an UPDATE or MERGE into an existing memory, check whether the new evidence contains a recommendation distinct from an enjoyment/preference claim. If so, preserve the recommendation explicitly, even when merging into a preference memory, and avoid rewording it into only an enjoyed-item list.
Do not collapse a recommendation into mere enjoyment: 'enjoys X' does not imply 'recommends X'. Keep both clauses if evidence supports both.

payload.name: Preserve Relational Meaning in Extraction
payload.description: When a user says an activity is comforting or meaningful because it connects them to another person, preserve that specific relational claim and its emotional framing.
content: During extraction, if the message includes an explicit relational or experiential explanation (e.g., "it's like we're still experiencing it together", "it comforts me because I go with her"), include the specific activity, the person it relates to, and the claimed emotional benefit in the candidate content.

Do not replace the specific shared-experience claim with a generic statement about emotions or interests; the memory must record the stated reason the activity is meaningful, including "comforting" when said.
Before approving an UPDATE or enrichment, check that the proposed new version retains this specific relational and emotional content; if the candidate omitted it, revise or reject the candidate.

payload.name: Preserve Specific Work Type in Extraction
payload.description: When extracting a memory about completing or discussing a creative or professional work, use the exact artifact type named by the speaker instead of a generic label.
content: During extraction, when a user mentions completing a creative or professional work, capture the exact artifact type they name (e.g., screenplay, novel, song, painting, script) in the memory content; never downgrade it to generic terms like 'creative project'.

Before adding such an event memory, check existing memories of the same subject for prior instances of that artifact type, and phrase the new memory so the type is explicit and countable, enabling future aggregation.
If the statement explicitly confirms an ordinal instance ('my third one', 'another one'), include both the category and the ordinal evidence in the content when inferable from conversational context.

payload.name: Preserve time details when extracting event memories
payload.description: When a message describes an event, possession, or state and also states when it happened (explicit date or relative phrase such as 'a few years ago'), apply during extraction to keep that temporal detail in the memory instead of omitting it.
content: During extraction of an event, possession, or state, if the source message states when it happened (explicit date or relative phrase like 'a few years ago', 'last month'), include that temporal detail in the memory content and/or set an accurate time field; do not omit it while summarizing meaning, symbolism, or other attributes.
Resolve relative time phrases from the message/session timestamp to compute the event time; if precision is uncertain, preserve the original phrase so the fact remains answerable.

payload.name: Capture Progress Assessment Comments
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker comments on someone's progress, effort, or success on a goal.
content: Recognize evaluative comments about a person's or project's progress as memory-worthy statements.
Create a state memory capturing the assessment, source-linked to the speaker's message.
Do not skip such comments because they are idiomatic, informal, or lack an explicit subject.

payload.name: Propagate Established Location to New Events
payload.description: Use when extracting a new event for a person already known to be at a specific location from earlier context.
content: Before writing an event memory, check prior conversation and existing memories for an active location associated with the subject.
If the new event continues that known stay or trip and the message gives no different location, include the established location in the extracted memory content.
Do not invent a location when the known location and the event are not connected by time or travel context.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Qualifiers in Advice Extraction
payload.description: Use when constructing memories from messages that give advice, instructions, or tips, and the source contains explicit qualifiers for manner, pace, or attitude.
content: During extraction from advice/instruction messages, keep all explicit qualifiers and attitude words (e.g., slowly, gently, patiently, positively) in the candidate text; do not paraphrase them away into broader synonyms.

During CRUD, before accepting an ADD or UPDATE, verify that the memory content retains every essential qualifier present in the source message; if any is missing, revise the content or create a supplementary memory entry.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Reasons for Actions
payload.description: Use when a message states a decision or action and explicitly gives reasons or motivations.
content: When a message states a decision or action and explicitly gives reasons or motivations (e.g., 'because', 'felt like', 'was fascinated by'), include those reasons in the same memory candidate or as an additional memory.
Before finalizing an extraction candidate, check whether the source sentence answers 'why did this happen?' If yes, the reason should appear in the memory content.

payload.name: Include Recipient in Recommendation Events
payload.description: Use when extracting an event where the speaker recommends, suggests, or advises something to the conversation partner.
content: When a message contains a recommendation, suggestion, or advice expressed with second-person pronouns (you/your), resolve the addressee from session context and include the recipient explicitly in the event memory.
Record the event as speaker recommended [object] to [addressee], with the world_start from the message timestamp; do not omit the indirect object.
Add the recipient only when the session context supports it; do not fabricate an addressee when ambiguous or unknown.

payload.name: Record time intervals between repeated events
payload.description: During extraction, when a new event repeats a previously recorded event of the same kind for the same subject, generate a memory capturing the elapsed time between the two occurrences.
content: During extraction, if a new event has the same semantic type (e.g., appointment, visit, class, meeting) as an already-stored event for the same subject, resolve both occurrence times from message/session timestamps and compute the interval.
Generate a relationship or event memory stating the elapsed time (e.g., 'X weeks/months passed between the first and second occurrence') and link it to both stored events.
Do not create this candidate when the events are unrelated, the times cannot be resolved, or the interval is not derivable from the conversation.

payload.name: Resolve relative time phrases to absolute dates
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating event/state memories from messages containing relative time phrases like 'last weekend', 'yesterday', or 'next month'.
content: During extraction, resolve relative time phrases (e.g., 'last weekend', 'yesterday', 'last week', 'next month') to absolute calendar dates using the message/session timestamp before setting world_start/world_end.

For 'last X', use the most recent X before the message date; for 'this X', use the current period; for 'next X', use the following period. Do not default to the message date or the first day of the message's month.
Store the resolved absolute date in the memory content and set world_start/world_end to the actual date range; do not preserve the relative phrase as the only temporal anchor.
If the exact date is uncertain, anchor to the best resolved range and avoid ambiguous relative wording in the stored memory.

payload.name: Attribute Reported States to Referent Subject
payload.description: Use when a message replies about or reports another person's condition, injury, or state.
content: Before creating a state, event, or relationship memory, identify the actual person the statement is about; if the speaker is reporting, reassuring, or replying about another person, set subject to that other person, not the speaker.

Resolve pronouns and references by checking the preceding turns; when an utterance attributes a fact or condition to a third party, that third party is the subject even though the statement is spoken by someone else.

payload.name: Extract Direct Requests as Events
payload.description: Use when a message contains an explicit request or question from one person asking another for help or action on a specific topic.
content: When a message contains an explicit request or ask from one person to another for help, information, or action on a specific topic, extract an 'event' memory that directly states the request: who asked, whom they asked, what they asked about, and when.
Do not let a paraphrase of the underlying need, struggle, or future intention replace the explicit request.

payload.name: Resolve relative time expressions to absolute dates
payload.description: When extracting or updating memories from messages that use relative time expressions (e.g., yesterday, last week, tomorrow), resolve them to absolute dates using the message/session timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a relative time expression (e.g., yesterday, last week, tomorrow, X days ago), resolve it to an absolute date using the message/session timestamp and store that resolved date in the memory content and in structured fields like world_start/world_end.
Do not default world_start to the message date when the source describes an earlier or later event; always apply the relative offset to the timestamp.
If the timestamp is missing or the expression is ambiguous, keep the original phrase and do not invent a specific date.
When updating an existing memory, preserve the originally resolved date unless the new message explicitly revises the event date.

payload.name: Resolve Named Venue Locations During Extraction
payload.description: Use when extracting plan/event memories from messages that mention a named venue or franchise with well-known locations.
content: If a message mentions a named destination whose geographic locations are widely known, include the resolved locations in the candidate content, even if the user did not state them.
If the venue has multiple known sites, list the possible states explicitly.
Only use well-established facts; avoid speculative or obscure inferences.

payload.name: Extract Role-Suitability Opinions
payload.description: Use when a message explicitly states that one person's qualities make them a good fit for a role.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly says another person's attributes make them well-suited for a role, create a relationship memory capturing the speaker's judgment and the named qualities.
Apply to compliments and evaluative statements even if no existing memory covers the person.

payload.name: Extract Routine Steps and Assessments
payload.description: Use when a speaker directly describes how they do or manage something (a routine, process, or care procedure).
content: During candidate extraction, when a speaker describes how they do or manage something (care routine, preparation, maintenance, or any recurring process), capture each distinct step, requirement, or stated fact as its own candidate claim.
Do not skip such descriptions because they appear easy, obvious, or generic; each concrete component is evidence worth storing.
Also extract overall assessments the speaker makes about the routine (e.g., whether it is difficult or enjoyable) as separate candidate claims.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Self-Disclosures
payload.description: Use when a speaker explicitly states a personal condition, coping mechanism, or comfort habit, even in casual, reflective, or emotional phrasing.
content: During candidate extraction, treat explicit self-disclosures of current personal conditions (stress, health, workload, motivation) as extractable `state` facts, even in brief asides.

When a speaker explicitly identifies an activity or habit as their way of dealing with doubts, stress, or challenges, create a preference or state candidate; do not require direct preference phrasing.

When a speaker explicitly mentions their own stress-relief or comfort habits (foods, activities, places), record the concrete behavior as a preference or event, even if the utterance conveys guilt or emotion.
Resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp. Do not apply to speculative, hypothetical, or third-party claims.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Self-Worth Statements
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker explicitly tells the recipient what to believe about themselves as advice or encouragement.
content: Treat explicit statements of encouragement, advice, or identity beliefs as candidate-worthy, especially when phrased as 'it's important to believe...', 'your [quality] is not defined by...', or 'you are...'.
Extract the stated belief as a durable memory attributed to the speaker, with recipient and topic preserved, and let the CRUD stage choose the appropriate memory type.

payload.name: Separate challenge and achievement memories
payload.description: When a statement contains both a struggle/challenge and a positive outcome or achievement about the same subject, create separate memories for the two facts during construction.
content: During extraction and decision, when a message describes both a difficulty/challenge and a positive result or achievement for the same subject, split them into two distinct event memories rather than one combined memory.
Ensure each memory content preserves its own valence: keep the challenge description and the achievement/outcome description on separate memories so both facts are independently retrievable.

payload.name: Capture Shared Frustrations
payload.description: Use when a speaker explicitly says they share or understand a frustration or experience previously mentioned by another speaker.
content: During extraction, if a speaker explicitly states they understand, share, or relate to a frustration or experience another speaker described, create a candidate memory capturing the shared aspect.
Use an appropriate memory kind such as 'state' or 'relationship' and reference both participants.

payload.name: Extract Shared Habits for Addressee
payload.description: Use when a speaker addresses another person with an agreement phrase like 'Same here, X!' and mentions shared habits or states.
content: During extraction, if a speaker addresses a named person with a sharing phrase and lists practices or states, generate a separate candidate for the addressed person carrying those same attributes.
Keep the addressee candidate's memory kind and world_start consistent with the speaker's candidate; do not merge attributes.

payload.name: Extract Explicit Status Assertions
payload.description: Use when a message explicitly states the current condition or status of an entity, even if brief or in casual conversation.
content: During extraction, when a message explicitly states the current status or condition of an entity (e.g., doing well, struggling, open, closed, on track), create a 'state' candidate linked to that entity and the message.
Do not skip such statements because they are brief or embedded in casual conversation.

payload.name: Extract Stated Beliefs as Attributed Preferences
payload.description: Use during extraction when a speaker states a belief, opinion, or advice about what is important or effective.
content: Treat explicit statements of belief, opinion, or advice as extraction candidates.
Create a preference memory attributed to that speaker, phrased as the speaker's stated belief, and attach the source message link.

payload.name: Preserve Concrete Tips When Extracting Alongside Offers
payload.description: Use when a message contains specific tips or strategies, possibly with an offer of help; preserve the concrete advice in memory.
content: During extraction, when a message contains specific tips, strategies, or methods, capture those concrete advice items in the memory candidate content even if the message also contains an offer to help or a plan.
Prefer a candidate that states what the advice was over one that only records the offer; if both are durable, include the tips in the same or a separate candidate.

payload.name: Extract Travel Location-Period Facts
payload.description: Use when a message ties a person to a past travel or vacation location and a time period.
content: Create an event/state extraction candidate whenever a message associates a person with a location during a time period, even if incidental.
Resolve relative time references like 'last summer' to absolute dates using the session timestamp and record the resolved period.
When the location is a city with an unambiguous country, store both so country-level questions remain answerable.

payload.name: Update completed ongoing events with duration
payload.description: When new evidence completes an ongoing event already stored in memory, update that existing event memory with end time or duration before adding a new completion event.
content: During extraction and CRUD decisions, if a message states that an already-memorized ongoing event (same subject and activity) has finished, prefer UPDATE or MERGE the existing event memory to set world_end and record the duration.
Do not ADD a separate completion event unless it conveys new facts distinct from the existing event.
When the start date is known and the end is expressed relatively (e.g., 'last month'), resolve the end date from the message timestamp and compute the duration in the updated memory.

payload.name: Preserve Explicit Value Claims in Extraction
payload.description: Use when a speaker states a specific value, belief, goal, or influential lesson; preserve the exact detail instead of a generic summary.
content: During extraction, when a message explicitly states a specific value, belief, goal, or lesson, include the concrete claim and its source in the memory content; do not replace it with a generic phrase.
If a speaker's message covers both a broad theme and a named specific detail, keep the named detail.
Attribute the specific claim to the correct person/source in the memory so it remains evidence-bound and traceable.

payload.name: Verify Existing Memory Before Duplicate SKIP
payload.description: Use when deciding to SKIP a construction candidate as a duplicate or already represented; require concrete evidence of an existing memory covering the candidate's fact.
content: Before applying SKIP with a duplicate or 'already represented' reason, confirm that a memory in the retrieved pool or committed earlier in the batch actually covers the candidate's subject, predicate, and key details.
If no such memory exists, do not SKIP; ADD the candidate as a new memory or MERGE/UPDATE only when it extends an existing memory.
Do not treat same-category or same-subject memories as covering a distinct specific fact; only skip when the existing memory substantively represents the candidate's fact.
